messages:
maria: heads-up — starting ~10:04 UTC we saw repeated tail-latency spikes on eu-west1-rack18. NIC tx_queue depth > 50k, kvcache miss rate jumped ~8x, a few slices showing 5–10% higher p99.

ops-bot: alert: net-queue-saturation eu-west1-rack18 (#alerts=4). Link: https://intra/alerts/6172

aj: any recent change to warm pool / kvcache eviction? logs?

maria: none that I know. quick sample: 
```
net.tx_queue: 52000
kvcache.miss_per_min: 4800 -> 38000
proc: tenant-42 qps: 2200 -> 18k
```

kai: my hunch: big tenant doing KV fanout (mapper/scan) and saturating NIC + IRQ, causing soft-affinity spill and eviction storms. pattern matches last month when irq_balance drifted.

lucas: could we do an emergency per-tenant clamp via eBPF to stop the immediate saturation? small low-risk shaping is quick.

aj: eBPF ingress/egress shaping + IRQ-affinity changes are lower-risk than a forced drain. runbook for shaping?

maria: propose immediate two-stage mitigation:
- 1) attach per-tenant token-bucket (5m) via eBPF to cap TX rate
- 2) async prewarm job to fetch hot prefixes into kvcache on standby warm-pool
- 3) if still bad after 15m, carve out a dedicated warm-pool slice for tenant-42 (canary first)

kai: I can drop a small bpftrace snippet + prewarm job. prewarm should iterate top-500 prefixes in 30s windows to avoid spike.

lucas: cost note — dedicated warm-pool carveout ~2–4% region GPU usage. prefer shaping+prewarm first.

aj: agreed. I'll run a canary: shape tenant-42 in rack18 at 80% TX cap + run prewarm for 10m. monitor p99, tx_queue, kvcache.hit_rate.

maria: ops-oncall approval required for carveout if shaping fails. @ops-oncall PTAL.

ops-bot: acknowledged by ops-oncall at 10:18 UTC — experiment id: exp-6172223.

kai: quick config example to attach a token bucket (conceptual):
```
# using tc (conceptual); we'll use eBPF variant in prod
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 10
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 8gbit burst 64k
# filter per-tenant ip/netmatch -> class 1:10
```

lucas: follow-ups: add telemetry tags so we can graph before/after automatically: [kvcache:hot_prefix_hit, nic:irq_balance_shift, tenant:shaping_applied]. I will PR the runbook with the eBPF snippet after the canary.

maria: canary started at 10:22 UTC. will post p99 numbers in ~10m. :thumbsup:

aj: if shaping stabilizes p99 < target we keep shaping as a short-term control and plan carveout during next maintenance window. if not, the 15m carveout play is ready.

kai: notes: add a guard in prewarm to back off if kvcache write amplification > 3x to avoid creating a new storm.

lucas: adding cost/impact labels to the experiment. thanks team.

maria: results: canary reduced net.tx_queue to ~12k and kvcache.miss_per_min down to 6k at 10:35 UTC. looks promising. keeping shaping for now and scheduling a 1hr postmortem tomorrow.
